pages.title: Flows
pages._note: Ordinary index over a NAMED SOURCE, not a custom page. A flow lives in OpenRegister's own native flow table rather than a register/schema pair, so an object-backed index had nothing to address and this used to be type:custom over FlowsIndex.vue. Named index sources (nextcloud-vue 2.20.0) close that: config.entitySource names the collection and the index loads it. Columns are stated here rather than left to the source's defaults because this is the ENGINE's cross-app surface — it passes no app filter and so needs the `app` column, which a leaf app's own flow list does not. Migrating also fixes a dead listener: FlowsIndex bound @rowClick while CnIndexPage emits row-click, so opening a flow by clicking its row never worked here. `rowRoute` names the flowDetail page (a route NAME, not a path): without it a named-source page has no schema, so CnPageRenderer never auto-wired editOpensDetail and row Edit opened an EMPTY modal instead of the flow editor.

pages.title: Flow
pages._note: The shared `flow` page type: a direct-manipulation canvas over a node/edge document is not expressible as a widget grid, and the built-in detail type is record-shaped — but that no longer requires a custom page. CnFlowEditorPage mounts the same CnFlowDetail canvas this app wrapped by hand, including the router.replace that lets a newly created flow pick up its server-assigned id. Controls live in the sidebar so the canvas gets full width, and both halves share useFlowStore.

pages.title: Tasks
pages._note: The fleet task inbox (flow-task-inbox-projections 5.1): an ordinary index over the NAMED `tasks` source (nextcloud-vue 2.30.0, cn-tasks-entity-source). The source supplies columns, the scope quick filters and the row click, which leaves the SPA for /apps/openregister/flow-tasks/{uuid} by full URL — served below by flow-task-detail. Like `flows`, this is the engine's cross-app surface; the source's own defaults fit it, so no columns are restated here.

observability._note: OpenRegister dogfoods its own AppHost observability engine (ADR-040). These descriptors reproduce the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index in appinfo/routes.php, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names, types and label keys match the pre-adoption contract; documented intentional improvements are the added health `app` field, the implicit `nextcloud_version` info label, and the objects_total register/schema labels now carrying numeric ids (engine tableCount groupBy) rather than titles.

steps.title: Welcome to OpenRegister
steps.body: OpenRegister is the data foundation the other apps build on. Everything they store lives here, in registers you define. This tour walks the three ideas that make it work: a register, a schema, and the objects that result.
A register is a container with a purpose, like a filing cabinet for one domain. Apps address one by its slug, so the slug is a contract other apps depend on.
Create one and give it a slug you will not want to change later. Renaming a register slug breaks every app that addresses it by name, so it is worth a moment of thought now.
A schema is the shape of one kind of thing inside a register. It is JSON Schema, so validation, defaults and required fields all come from the same definition.
Add a schema to the register you just made. Once it exists, every object stored against it is validated on write, which is why bad data tends not to reach the other apps.
Search and views read across registers and schemas at once. This is where the objects your apps write actually surface, and where you check that a write landed the way you expected.

steps.title: Where the automation lives
steps.body: Flows are what happens without anyone clicking: an object that gets stamped on save, a downstream app told when a record changes. This is where you read and edit them. Nothing to build now.

steps.title: That is the foundation
steps.body: Register, schema, objects: define the container, define the shape, and every app on the stack can read and write it through the same API. The rest of OpenRegister, from audit trails to data quality, hangs off those three.
